Package de.schladebeck.fx.grid.model

package de.schladebeck.fx.grid.model

Where a Grid's data comes from. A GridModel is a rectangle of values addressed by row and column; the grid asks it only for the cells it shows, so the data can live anywhere.

Ready-made models

Model Data Size
ListGridModel a list of objects, one per row, a column per getter or record component what fits in memory
ComputedGridModel a function of row and column any, no memory
PagedGridModel pages loaded on demand in the background, e.g. from a database any, a few pages in memory
TreeGridModel a tree of objects; the children of an expanded one follow it the opened part of the tree

ListGridModel.of(ObservableList) shows a JavaFX ObservableList and follows every change of it, including changes inside items that the list reports through an extractor.

Writing a model

Anything else is a small subclass of AbstractGridModel, for example one object per column instead of per row:

GridModel laptops = new AbstractGridModel() {
    public int getRowCount() { return properties.size(); }
    public int getColumnCount() { return items.size(); }
    public Object getValueAt(int row, int column) { return properties.get(row).apply(items.get(column)); }
    public String getRowName(int row) { return propertyNames.get(row); }
};

Rows and columns are symmetric: both have names, and each cell may hold a value of any type. A model that can sort better than the grid, such as a database query, overrides GridModel.sortRows(List, IntFunction): it gets the SortKeys, one per sort column.

Threads

The grid reads models on the JavaFX application thread. Changes from other threads go through AbstractGridModel.applyChange(Runnable): it runs the change right away on the JavaFX thread, and otherwise queues it. Queued changes run on the JavaFX thread in order, in batches of about 8 ms. Before the toolkit starts, changes run right away on the calling thread. The changing methods and the builders of the ready-made models do this already; builders of your own use AbstractGridModel.applySetup(Runnable), so a model can be set up on any thread before a grid shows it. The grid rejects events fired from another thread. An ObservableList shown with ListGridModel.of(ObservableList) changes on the JavaFX thread only, like any list shown in a JavaFX control.

Events

Models report changes with GridModelEvents: rows inserted, deleted or updated, all rows changed (DATA), or everything including the columns changed (STRUCTURE). The grid repaints only if a changed row is on screen, keeps the visible rows in place when rows are inserted or deleted above them, and moves the selection with its rows.

Implementation notes

ListGridModel, PagedGridModel and TreeGridModel share the column logic (names, getters, update functions, row names) through the package-private ItemColumns. The items stay with each model.

A ListGridModel showing an ObservableList reads a copy of it. A list change can come in several parts (as from removeAll); each part goes into the copy right before its event, so every event matches the rows the grid reads. The list holds the model through a weak listener, so a list that lives on does not keep grids alive.

PagedGridModel requests a page when a cell of it is asked for and not loaded. Requests are served newest first, a few at a time, so fast scrolling loads what is on screen now. Loaded pages arrive through applyChange and fire an update for their rows, which repaints only if they are on screen. A reload or a new sort order starts a new generation; pages still loading for an older one are dropped when they arrive.
